title: Compact-support finiteness for arbitrary finite rings and a finite-type target
statement:
Let $k$ be any field, let $Y$ be a scheme of finite type over $k$, let $X$ be a scheme and let $f:X\to Y$ be of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose a compactification $c=(j,q)$ is supplied: $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{q}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion, $q$ proper and $qj=f$ [def-nagata-compactification]. Then $f$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $\Lambda$ be any finite commutative ring. On ordinary small étale sites, with module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], put $Rf_!^c=Rq_*\circ D(j_!)$, using extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and ordinary total derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For every $M\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes],
$$Rf_!^c M\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda).$$
Moreover, there exists $N\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, independent of $M,a,b$, such that if $\mathcal H^i(M)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$, then $\mathcal H^i(Rf_!^cM)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b+N]$. Neither $X$ nor $Y$ is required to be separated over $k$. No finite Tor amplitude of $M$, invertibility of the exponent of $\Lambda$, or restriction to a local coefficient ring is assumed.

proof.text: First check the geometric hypotheses needed below. The field $k$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] successively to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $f:X\to Y$, and $q:\overline X\to Y$; $q$ is of finite type by the definition of properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus $Y,X,\overline X$ are Noetherian, hence quasi-compact and, by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], quasi-separated. The morphisms $f$ and $q$ are locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth]. They are quasi-compact by finite type and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), since their sources are quasi-separated. Thus $f$ is of finite presentation. Also $j$ is quasi-compact by that same permanence lemma, since $X$ is quasi-compact and $\overline X$ is quasi-separated. These arguments require no separatedness over $k$.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01TX (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation); properties.tex Tag 01OY; schemes.tex Tags 03GI and 01KV

proof.text: The open immersion $j$ identifies $X$ with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Therefore $X\times_{\overline X}X\cong X$ and its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence a closed immersion. It follows directly from [def-weil-proper-morphism] that $j$ is separated. The proper map $q$ is separated by the same definition. By the composition clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], $f=qj$ is separated.

source.place: Tags 01L4 (lemma-monomorphism-separated), 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence), clause (1); the open-immersion case is the displayed diagonal argument

proof.text: Extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and exact functors commute with cohomology by [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](c). Hence, for $L=D(j_!)M$, one has $\mathcal H^r(L)=j_!\mathcal H^r(M)$; in particular $L$ is bounded below and has the same cohomological interval as $M$. To compare the two derived conventions, the module sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and admit K-injective resolutions by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The functor $q_*$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. Therefore [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility], applied to $q_*$, identifies its bounded-below derived functor on $L$ with its unbounded total right derived functor on $L$. All subsequent bounded-below computations consequently compute the functor $Rq_*D(j_!)$ specified in the statement.

By [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], $M$ is bounded below with constructible cohomology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-compactification-constructibility] to $f$ and the supplied compactification $(j,q)$. Its hypotheses are verified in steps 1 and 2: both endpoints are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $f$ is separated and finitely presented, and $j$ is quasi-compact. Its coefficient hypothesis is precisely that $\Lambda$ is a finite commutative ring. It yields constructibility of every $\mathcal H^r(Rq_*j_!M)$. By step 3 this is the required unbounded-derived compact-support output.

Since $q$ is proper, it is of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $Y$ is quasi-compact by step 1. Thus [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] supplies $d\geq0$ bounding the dimensions of every scheme-theoretic fibre of $q$. Fix this $d$ once and for all, and put $N=2d$. This choice depends on the supplied compactification and not on $M$ or its cohomological interval.

Let $F$ be any $\Lambda$-module sheaf on $\overline X_{\mathrm{et}}$. The finiteness of $\Lambda$ gives a positive integer $m$ with $m1_\Lambda=0$, so $mF=0$ and its underlying abelian sheaf $U(F)$ is torsion. Apply [lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound] to $q$ and $U(F)$ to obtain $R^p q_*U(F)=0$ for $p>2d$. By [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison], this is the underlying abelian sheaf of the module higher direct image $R^p q_*F$. A module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf is zero. Hence $R^p q_*F=0$ for $p>2d$, uniformly for all $F$. This uses no invertibility of $m$ on any scheme.

proof.text:
Suppose $\mathcal H^r(M)=0$ for $r
otin[a,b]$. By step 3, $L=D(j_!)M$ has the same vanishing. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to the left exact module direct image $q_*$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact] between the Grothendieck abelian module sheaf categories [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]. It gives a spectral sequence $E_2^{p,r}=R^p q_*\mathcal H^r(L)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+r}(Rq_*L)$, with $E_2^{p,r}=0$ for $p<0$ and a finite exhaustive separated abutment filtration in every total degree. Step 6 gives $E_2^{p,r}=0$ for $p>2d$, and the hypothesis gives zero for $r
otin[a,b]$. Thus a nonzero term must have $a\leq p+r\leq b+2d$. Outside this interval every associated graded of the finite filtration is zero, so the abutment is zero. By step 3 this proves $\mathcal H^i(Rf_!^cM)=0$ for $i
otin[a,b+N]$, with the fixed $N=2d\geq0$.

proof.text: For each $M\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ choose a finite cohomological interval $[a,b]$ using [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Step 7 bounds the output in $[a,b+N]$, and step 4 makes each of its cohomology sheaves constructible. These are exactly the two conditions in that definition for $Rf_!^cM\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$. The same $N$ works for every input and every proposed interval. The zero ring and empty schemes cause no exception: their module complexes are zero and the bound still holds.
